## Claims
- [source-backed] A bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\in S_n\) has \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\); the source defines \(J_v=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 68-78]
- [source-backed] The coefficient ring is \(\Lambda=\Lambda(x_1,x_2,\ldots)\) with integral coefficients, \(I_{r,n-r}=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_\lambda:\lambda\nsubseteq(n-r)^r\}\), and \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}=:\overline\Lambda\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 89-94]
- [source-backed] Theorem 1.2 assumes a bigrassmannian \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\in S_n\), defines \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), and \(b=\min(i,j)\), and concludes that \(J_v\), as an ideal of \(\overline\Lambda\), is minimally generated by \(\{\overline{s}_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\); “minimality” means no generator can be removed. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 95-110]
- [source-backed] Corollary 4.6 restates minimality for the same family, while Remark 4.7 records the transposed family \(\{\overline{s}_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) and says that transposing the arguments would prove its minimality. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 503-512]
- [source-backed] The requested theorem-level extraction is established from the supplied full-text passage; the cited theorem itself explicitly concludes minimality only for the first displayed family, and no stronger implication is asserted here. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 95-110]

## Strategy
Extracted the definitions, integral coefficient setting, exact theorem hypotheses, generating family, and conclusion; separately recorded the transposed-family remark.

## Gaps
No supplied passage states the transposed family’s minimality as part of Theorem 1.2; the source presents it in a remark.
